questions.q: In the NIH depletion-repletion study, what happened to fasting plasma vitamin C when the daily dose rose from 200 to 2,500 mg?
options: It rose only from about 68 to 85 µmol/L
It roughly doubled
It rose tenfold, in proportion to the dose
It fell, because high doses are toxic to the transporter
questions.why: The curve is sigmoid: 200 mg is the first dose beyond the steep part, complete plasma saturation comes at 1,000 mg, and the plateau has a shallow slope.

questions.q: At what daily intake were neutrophils, monocytes and lymphocytes saturated with vitamin C in men?
options: About 1,000 mg a day
About 100 mg a day, at 14 times the plasma concentration
About 2,300 mg a day, Pauling's optimum
They never saturate; more always enters
questions.why: Women's plasma and cells saturated at 400 mg; the immune cells the marketing talks about are full at food intake.

questions.q: What happens to a single oral dose of vitamin C above about 500 mg?
options: It is stored in the liver for later
It is fully absorbed and raises tissue stores proportionally
Absorption falls and the absorbed surplus is excreted once plasma passes the renal threshold
It is converted to vitamin E
questions.why: The renal threshold sits near 86 µmol/L in men and 72 in women; at pharmacological levels clearance approaches the glomerular filtration rate.

questions.q: What peak plasma level does 1.25 g of vitamin C produce by mouth, and by vein?
options: The same, about 500 µmol/L either way
About 885 by mouth and 135 by vein
About 13,400 µmol/L either way
About 135 µmol/L by mouth and about 885 by vein
questions.why: The maximum tolerable oral regimen is modelled to top out near 220 µmol/L against 13,400 for 50 g intravenously; oral and intravenous vitamin C are different drugs.

questions.q: How does kiwifruit-derived vitamin C compare with synthetic ascorbic acid in steady-state human studies?
options: They are identical in plasma, white cells and muscle
Kiwifruit vitamin C is absorbed about 35 % better
Synthetic is absorbed better because it has no fibre
Kiwifruit vitamin C is retained three times longer
questions.why: The 35 % bioflavonoid claim is one eight-person single-dose study from 1988; every steady-state comparison finds no difference.

questions.q: What does Cochrane find for daily vitamin C and colds in the general community?
options: Half as many colds
Incidence RR 0.97 (0.94 to 1.00), colds about 8 % shorter in adults, and no consistent effect when started at onset
Colds prevented entirely at 1 g a day
Colds a third shorter when started at the first sneeze
questions.why: In 10,708 community participants the incidence effect is near nothing; the duration effect needs daily use all season.

questions.q: In which group did vitamin C halve the rate of colds?
options: Office workers in winter
Children in daycare
598 marathon runners, skiers and sub-arctic soldiers under brief heavy exertion, in small old trials
Everyone who took at least 1 g a day
questions.why: The subgroup RR is 0.48 (0.35 to 0.64); a 674-recruit trial at 2 g a day was null, so the pattern is not universal.

questions.q: On what did Linus Pauling base his 2.3 g a day optimum?
options: A randomised trial he ran in 1970
The NIH saturation studies
Measured leukocyte ascorbate in his own laboratory
An evolutionary argument about ancestral diets and the synthesis rate of animals that make their own vitamin C
questions.why: He also pooled four small pre-1970 trials and proposed a 250 to 4,000 mg band; he ran no cold trial, and the 2,349-person Toronto trial found no dose-response.

questions.q: What did 500 mg of vitamin C a day do to cardiovascular events, cancer and mortality over eight to nine years in 22,812 people?
options: Nothing: events HR 0.99 and RR 1.02, cancer 1.01, cataract 1.02, mortality 1.07
Cut events by a fifth
Cut cancer by a third
Raised mortality significantly
questions.why: The Physicians' Health Study II and the Women's Antioxidant Cardiovascular Study are the two trials that tested exactly this decision.

questions.q: Does vitamin C alone carry the mortality signal seen for antioxidant supplements as a class?
options: Yes, it raises mortality 5 %
No: RR 1.02 (0.98 to 1.07) across 29 low-bias trials; the signal comes from β-carotene, vitamin A and vitamin E
Yes, it lowers mortality 10 %
The question has never been studied
questions.why: The 2007 and 2012 antioxidant meta-analyses both clear vitamin C in either direction.

questions.q: How much extra urinary oxalate does 1,000 mg of ascorbic acid produce?
options: None; the oxalate rise is an assay artefact
About 500 mg, complete conversion
About 6 to 13 mg a day, 1.2 to 1.8 % of the dose's millimoles, in stone formers and non-formers alike
About 1 mg, too little to measure
questions.why: Controlled studies with preservatives, EDTA and isotopes excluded in-vitro conversion and still found 20 to 60 % rises at 1 to 2 g.

questions.q: What did the large cohorts find for kidney stones and vitamin C intake?
options: Everyone at 1,000 mg had twice the stones
No association in anyone
Women at 1,000 mg had more stones, men did not
Men at 1,000 mg or more had about 40 to 90 % more symptomatic stones; women showed nothing, and food-only intake nothing in either sex
questions.why: HPFS RR 1.41, the pooled Harvard cohorts HR 1.43, Swedish supplement users HR 1.92; about one extra stone per 80 men a decade.

questions.q: What do the famous 'antioxidants blunt training' trials have in common?
options: They combined vitamin C with vitamin E, and pooled across 18 trials the combination changed neither VO2max, endurance, lean mass nor strength
They all used vitamin C alone at 200 mg
They all found VO2max gains halved
They were all in elite athletes
questions.why: Ristow, Paulsen, Bjørnsen and Morrison all used C plus E; the vitamin-C-only training evidence is thin in both directions.

questions.q: How much do antioxidant supplements reduce muscle soreness?
options: By about half
About 0.2 to 0.5 cm on a 10 cm scale, below the 1.4 cm a person can notice
By 3 to 4 cm on a 10 cm scale
They abolish soreness at 3 g a day
questions.why: Across 50 trials the effect is statistically detectable and not noticeable; vitamin C alone protected neither force nor range of motion.

questions.q: What happened in the only randomised blinded trials of oral vitamin C megadoses?
options: Survival quadrupled, as Pauling had reported
COVID symptoms resolved two days sooner
They were null: 10 g a day in 250 cancer patients and 8 g a day in 214 COVID-19 outpatients
They were stopped early for benefit
questions.why: The Mayo trials found overlapping survival curves; COVID A to Z found 5.5 against 6.7 days to half-symptom reduction, P = .45.

questions.q: What did the LOVIT trial find for intravenous vitamin C in 872 septic adults?
options: Mortality cut from 40 % to 8 %
No difference in anything
Faster recovery with no harm
More death or persistent organ dysfunction, 44.5 % against 38.5 %, RR 1.21
questions.why: The 2,590-patient COVID-19 trials were also stopped for harm and futility; the HAT-protocol trials were null.

questions.q: What happened when smokers took 1 g of vitamin C a day for eight weeks after a single 2 g dose had improved their artery dilation?
options: Plasma stayed at 92 µmol/L and dilation was back to 3.9 %, no sustained effect
Dilation kept improving month by month
Plasma fell below baseline
Dilation improved only in non-smokers
questions.why: Acute doses and infusions dilate sick arteries for a couple of hours; the chronic-only pooled effect is SMD 0.25 with a lower bound of 0.02.

questions.q: What does vitamin C do to blood pressure?
options: A 15 mmHg fall that persists for years
About 4/1.5 mmHg lower in eight-week trials at 500 mg, more in hypertensives, and nothing over five years
Nothing at any dose or duration
A rise in hypertensives
questions.why: The only five-year trial found identical rises on 500 and 50 mg a day, and no trial links the short-term fall to events.

questions.q: What blunted the HDL rise from simvastatin plus niacin in the HATS trial?
options: Vitamin C alone at 500 mg
Vitamin E alone
A cocktail of vitamins E and C with β-carotene and selenium, so vitamin C cannot be singled out
The niacin itself
questions.why: Lipid effects of vitamin C are inconsistent: LDL −7.9 mg/dL in hypercholesterolaemic patients against an overall null in the larger synthesis.

questions.q: Why does the 20 % lower mortality per 20 µmol/L of plasma vitamin C not argue for a pill?
options: Because it was measured only in smokers
Because it reversed in women
Because the pill raised mortality in the same cohort
It is strongest in blood and weakest as intake, null in Mendelian randomisation, and read by its own authors as a fruit-and-vegetable marker
questions.why: Being the kind of person with high plasma ascorbate is not the same as swallowing ascorbate; the pill has never reproduced the gradient.

questions.q: Who gained measurable performance from 1 g of vitamin C a day for 30 days?
options: Men selected for the lowest plasma ascorbate, who gained 5.4 mL/kg/min of VO2max and 18.7 Nm of torque
Replete athletes
Everyone in the trial
Nobody
questions.why: This is repletion: low status, not high dose, is what the pill moves, and a 2026 n-of-1 series found no true responder structure.

questions.q: What is the one outcome-level cost shown for 1 g of vitamin C with vitamin E during resistance training?
options: Halved strength gains in young men
Lean-mass gain of 1.4 % against 3.9 % in 60- to 81-year-old men, with identical strength gains
Loss of muscle mass
No cost of any kind
questions.why: Marker blunting of PGC-1α, COX4 and SOD is real for the combination; Ristow's insulin-sensitivity result was not reproduced at 12 weeks.

questions.q: How strong is the human evidence that vitamin C alone blunts training adaptation?
options: Overwhelming: dozens of trials
Settled by the rat studies
Thin in both directions: five supplemented men behind the founding paper, a null trial at 1 g, a 1.3 ± 1.3 % effect and no trial at 200 mg
Settled by Cochrane
questions.why: Rats synthesise their own ascorbate and showed no blunting at 50 times the human dose; the textbook mechanism is chemically contested.

questions.q: What happened to the ultramarathon cortisol-attenuation finding in the largest, carbohydrate-fed, double-blind trial at the same 1,500 mg dose?
options: It doubled in size
It appeared only at 500 mg
It was confirmed in every outcome
It did not replicate: no effect on cortisol, cytokines, immune cells or oxidative markers
questions.why: The attenuation sits in three small South African studies; a 48 % smaller FEV1 fall in exercise-induced bronchoconstriction comes from 40 people.

questions.q: What share of US adults is biochemically deficient in vitamin C, and how has it changed?
options: About 7 %, unchanged between 2003 and 2018
About 30 % and rising
Under 1 %
About 50 %
questions.why: A quarter of low-income British men were deficient; inpatients run 28 %; produce three or more times a day kept Glasgow adults above the line.

questions.q: How much vitamin C do smokers and people over about 100 kg need to reach the same plasma level as others?
options: The same 90 mg
Roughly double: about 165 mg a day for smokers and 155 for the heavy, against 110 for everyone else
About 1,000 mg
Half as much, because they absorb more
questions.why: Radiotracer turnover shows smokers need at least 140 mg against about 100; their plasma runs a third lower at population level.

questions.q: What range does the expert requirement debate span, and why?
options: 500 to 2,000 mg a day
10 to 40 mg a day
75 to 200 mg a day, from leukocyte saturation, a 50 µmol/L mass balance and the plasma curve, all on the same data
2 to 8 g a day
questions.why: Every camp's number is reachable from food; no camp argues for more than 200 mg on pharmacokinetic grounds.

questions.q: Which plasma bands define vitamin C status, and what is the valid test?
options: Deficient below 100 µmol/L; a urine dipstick
Deficient below 50 µmol/L; a saliva test
There are no agreed bands
Deficient below 11.4 µmol/L, marginal at or below 23, adequate at or above 50, saturating above 65; fasting plasma in a promptly stabilised EDTA tube
questions.why: Plasma tracked intake with less variability than cells; urine and saliva were useless; unstabilised samples under-read.

questions.q: What is the honest summary of Ester-C and liposomal vitamin C?
options: Ester-C matches plain ascorbate in plasma and is gentler on the stomach; liposomal forms raise a single dose's exposure and nobody has measured whether the extra is kept
Both double tissue stores
Both are absorbed worse than plain ascorbic acid
Both have been shown to prevent colds
questions.why: The leukocyte claims come from manufacturer-run single-dose studies; the independent 250 mg comparison found no difference.

questions.q: How much vitamin C in a meal maximises non-haem iron absorption, and does the effect hold across a whole diet?
options: At least 1,000 mg; the effect is large everywhere
About 50 mg per meal; across a whole diet the effect is small, and adding it to iron tablets adds nothing
None; vitamin C blocks iron
About 500 mg; it doubles iron stores
questions.why: Food ascorbate equals crystals for iron; diagnosed iron overload is a precautionary reason to avoid supplements.

questions.q: What is the state of the evidence for intravenous vitamin C in cancer?
options: Proven to double survival in every cancer
Disproven entirely
A reproducible millimolar peroxide mechanism, zero single-agent responses in phase I, and one open-label 34-patient randomised trial awaiting replication
Approved as standard first-line therapy
questions.why: Four systematic reviews split on tone and agree there is no high-quality evidence of benefit; practitioners treat about 11,000 patients a year.

questions.q: What does it take for vitamin C to cause oxalate nephropathy?
options: Any dose above 100 mg
Only doses above 10 g a day
It has never happened
Usually two of three: intravenous grams, kidneys that cannot clear oxalate, or a gut that over-absorbs it
questions.why: Oral cases carry the second factor, at doses as low as 680 mg with chronic diarrhoea or 4 g on dialysis.

questions.q: What does 500 mg of vitamin C a day do to serum urate?
options: Lowers it about 0.35 mg/dL in healthy people and trivially in gout, where allopurinol lowered it eight times as much
Raises it
Lowers it as much as allopurinol
Nothing at all
questions.why: The gout-prevention association (RR 0.55 at 1,500 mg) is observational and untested in a trial.

questions.q: How certain is the glucose benefit of vitamin C in type 2 diabetes?
options: Settled: it lowers HbA1c 2 %
Small short trials show glucose and blood-pressure signals at 1,000 mg; the HbA1c estimate is graded very low certainty, and non-diabetics show nothing
Settled: it has no effect
Settled: it raises glucose
questions.why: One cohort of diabetic women showed higher cardiovascular mortality with supplemental vitamin C, so the question is open in both directions.

questions.q: What is the evidence that vitamin C prevents pneumonia?
options: A dozen large modern trials
The LOVIT trial
Three small trials with 37 events in 1940s to 1970s recruits and schoolboys, rated too weak for general use; the one good treatment trial used 200 mg in depleted elderly inpatients
The Toronto trial
questions.why: The treatment result is repletion in sick, depleted people, not a megadose effect.

questions.q: What is the 6 to 8 g dose-response hypothesis for colds based on?
options: A 2020 Cochrane review
The NIH saturation studies
A trial in 10,000 soldiers
Two 1970s trials whose own authors concluded the opposite, with no modern blinded test and two supporting meta-analyses retracted
questions.why: Karlowski attributed the effect to a broken blind; the Toronto authors found no dose-response and put the optimum below 250 mg.

questions.q: Why can the ASAP, WAVE and HATS trials not tell you what vitamin C does?
options: They combined it with vitamin E and other antioxidants, so no effect can be attributed to vitamin C alone
They used too little vitamin C to matter
They were all in children
They never measured vitamin C
questions.why: HOPE and HOPE-TOO, often cited as vitamin C trials, contained no vitamin C at all.

questions.q: What did the human iron-plus-vitamin C study show about pro-oxidant DNA damage?
options: Permanent doubling of DNA damage
A transient, baseline-dependent rise in some oxidised bases at six weeks that normalised by twelve
No measurement was possible
A fall in all oxidised bases at every dose
questions.why: Lipid peroxidation did not change at any oral dose in women held at steady state; no clinical harm has been tied to pro-oxidant chemistry.

questions.q: What is the evidence for 'rebound scurvy' after stopping high-dose vitamin C?
options: Hundreds of hospital cases
A Cochrane review
Two subjects whose urinary ascorbate dipped below baseline for 10 to 12 days, in a hypotheses journal; no clinical case
A randomised withdrawal trial
questions.why: The B12-destruction claim was an assay artefact refuted in 1976 and the warfarin interaction is one 1971 case against a 1975 negative study.

questions.q: Does vitamin C prevent cataract, macular degeneration or dementia?
options: Yes, all three
Yes for cataract only
Yes for dementia only
No: cataract HR 1.02, AMD RR 0.96 with high certainty, vitamin C alone null for Alzheimer's, and 25 % more cataract surgery in Swedish women on about a gram
questions.why: The AREDS benefit is for established macular degeneration with zinc added, not prevention.

questions.q: What does the eightfold collagen rise with vitamin C come from?
options: Cultured fibroblasts that started with no ascorbate at all; no oral trial links extra vitamin C to skin or collagen outcomes in replete adults
A trial in 500 adults taking 1 g a day
A wound-healing trial of vitamin C alone
Topical trials in smokers
questions.why: The hydroxylase cofactor role saturates at tissue concentrations that food reaches.

questions.q: What is the 2,000 mg upper level based on, and what does it miss?
options: Kidney-stone data from 2016
Osmotic diarrhoea, set in 2000 and defended by the supplement trade association; it predates the men's stone cohorts, whose signal sits below it
The LOVIT trial
Leukocyte saturation
questions.why: The NIH group set its own safe line below 1,000 mg on oxalate and urate excretion.

questions.q: For a non-smoking adult who eats produce several times a day, what does a vitamin C pill add?
options: A doubling of tissue stores
Protection from colds
About 10 µmol/L of plasma and a few hours of higher urinary output
A lower stone risk
questions.why: Two gold kiwifruit, or a red pepper with an orange, reach the 200 mg first dose beyond the curve; boiling vegetables costs 20 to 60 %.

questions.q: When does the 'get it from food' rule bend, and to what dose?
options: For everyone in winter, at 1,000 mg
Never
For athletes, at 3 g a day
For status, not dose: smokers, people over about 100 kg, low-produce eaters and anyone below 50 µmol/L are repletion cases at 100 to 200 mg; any pill belongs at 200 to 400 mg
questions.why: The one defensible pill use case is a short 0.5 to 1 g course around an ultramarathon or ski camp; not with vitamin E at 1 g during training.

questions.q: Who should never take gram doses of vitamin C?
options: Anyone with a prior calcium-oxalate stone, kidney disease or dialysis, malabsorption, chronic diarrhoea, G6PD deficiency (for infusions), iron overload, or on chemotherapy without the oncologist's agreement
Only children
Only people on warfarin
Nobody; it is water-soluble
questions.why: To know rather than guess, a fasting plasma ascorbate in a promptly stabilised EDTA tube at or above 50 µmol/L is adequate and above 65 saturating.
